messages.content: Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6.

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.content:
**Standard error (standard deviation of the sampling distribution)**  

\[
SE = \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}} = \frac{1.4}{\sqrt{40}}
\]

\[
\sqrt{40}\approx 6.3249 \;\;\Rightarrow\;\;
SE \approx \frac{1.4}{6.3249}\approx 0.221
\]

So the standard deviation of the null‑hypothesis test (i.e., the standard error of the sample mean) is **≈ 0.22**.
message.reasoning:
The user says "Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test" but likely they want the standard error or maybe the p-value? They provide sample mean 98.2, std dev 1.4, sample size 40, population mean 98.6. They ask to calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test. That might refer to the standard error of the mean under null: sigma/sqrt(n). But we don't know population sigma; we have sample std dev 1.4. So standard error = 1.4 / sqrt(40) ≈ 0.221. But maybe they want the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the sample mean under null: same as standard error. So answer: ~0.221.

But the tool is for calculating p-value. We could call it to compute p-value. But question: "Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test". Might be mis-specified. Could interpret as "calculate the standard error" which is the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the sample mean. So we can compute that manually. Provide explanation. Also mention that if we had population sigma, we would use that. But using sample sigma gives approximate SE.

Thus answer: Standard error = 1.4 / sqrt(40) ≈ 0.221. Provide steps.
